groups.reason: Both impose the same post-establishment integrity check: attacker modification of protected channel data must be detected and modified data must not be accepted as authentic. The complete-network-control wording supplies the attacker model for that same property, not a different implementation direction or outcome; the canonical evidence states the integrity property directly.

Both require encoding and decoding SignatureScheme.rsa_pkcs1_sha256 as 0x0401. They have the same field, value, bidirectional implementation check, and error outcome; the canonical requirement cites the primary-body enum.

Both apply the identical 0-through-32-octet structural bound to ServerHello.legacy_session_id_echo for encoding and parsing, with no distinct error outcome. The canonical requirement uses the direct primary-body field definition.
Both require encoding and decoding SignatureScheme.rsa_pss_rsae_sha384 as 0x0805. The field, value, direction, and outcome are identical; the canonical requirement cites the primary-body enum.

Both constrain the client-created ClientHello.cipher_suites list to record-protection/AEAD and HKDF-hash pairs the client supports. Constructing and offering the list are the same outbound check here, and neither member adds a different field, value, direction, or error outcome; the canonical requirement is the direct field definition.

This member is the broader check requiring supported_versions whenever sending a ServerHello. It is not equivalent to the TLS 1.3-negotiation/message-specific members, as confirmed by the known broader-versus-narrower conflict, so it remains self-canonical.

Both require a server's TLS 1.3 ServerHello to contain supported_versions and prohibit omission. Negotiating TLS 1.3 and the outbound message being a TLS 1.3 ServerHello identify the same server-side condition, direction, and outcome; the canonical requirement is the clearer direct normative primary-body statement.

This requirement is limited to encoding PskBinderEntry with a 32-through-255-octet payload. It does not contain the parser-direction check present in the unconditioned structural requirement, so it remains self-canonical.

This unconditioned structural field bound applies to serializer and parser behavior. A correct encoder with a parser that accepts an out-of-range PskBinderEntry can satisfy the encoding-only member but violate this one, so the broader bidirectional check remains distinct and self-canonical.

Both require encoding and decoding SignatureScheme.rsa_pss_rsae_sha256 as 0x0804. The field, value, bidirectional check, and outcome are identical; the canonical requirement cites the primary-body enum.
Both require encoding and decoding NamedGroup.ffdhe8192 as 0x0104. The field, value, bidirectional check, and outcome are identical; the canonical requirement cites the primary-body enum.

Both require encoding and decoding SignatureScheme.rsa_pss_rsae_sha512 as 0x0806. The field, value, bidirectional check, and outcome are identical; the canonical requirement cites the primary-body enum.

Both impose the same structural serializer/parser check that the encoded ClientHello.extensions vector has a byte length from 8 through 2^16-1. The field, bounds, direction, and outcome are identical; the canonical requirement uses the direct primary-body field definition.

Both require a conforming implementation's outbound ClientHello to contain supported_versions and prohibit omission. The condition, sender direction, extension-presence check, and outcome are equivalent; the canonical requirement cites the direct primary-body MUST statement.

Both require serializing UncompressedPointRepresentation.X as exactly coordinate_length octets. They cover the same X field, length value, encoding direction, and outcome; the canonical requirement cites the primary-body structure.
